tldr: The paper introduces GTA, a benchmark for evaluating general tool agents using human-written queries, real deployed tools, and multimodal inputs, revealing that current LLMs struggle with real-world tool use.
contributions: A tool-use benchmark with 229 human-designed, step-implicit, tool-implicit real-world tasks across four tool categories
An evaluation platform with 14 executable tools spanning perception, operation, logic, and creativity
Fine-grained evaluation metrics (InstAcc, ToolAcc, ArgAcc, SummAcc) and comprehensive analysis of 16 LLMs
methods: The authors designed 229 real-world tasks with human-written queries, authentic multimodal image inputs (spatial scenes, screenshots, tables, code snippets, handwritten materials), and executable tool chains using 14 tools across four categories. Dataset construction followed an exemplar-based pipeline where experts designed initial samples and human annotators expanded them with diversified scenarios. Two evaluation modes were used: step-by-step mode to assess fine-grained tool-use prediction, and end-to-end mode where models dynamically invoke tools to solve tasks. The benchmark was tested on 16 LLMs using the Lagent framework with ReAct prompting on an OpenCompass platform.
results: GTA contains 229 queries (172 with pure text answers, 57 with image answers), 252 image files, and 14 tools. Most questions use 2-3 tools with 2-4 steps. GPT-4 completes less than 50% of tasks in end-to-end evaluation, while most LLMs achieve below 25%. Perception+Logic and Perception+Operation are the most frequent tool combinations.
limitations: Web search tools may return variable results over time, though the authors mitigated this with time-constrained questions. Some queries were discarded when tools failed to provide accurate recognition (e.g., OCR inaccuracies). The benchmark focuses on tool-use evaluation rather than broader AGI capabilities, and end-to-end performance is low across all models, suggesting significant bottlenecks remain.
